2. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking quashing of the charge sheet dated 25.08.2019, summoning order dated 02.01.2020 as well as entire proceedings of Case No.576 of 2020 (State Vs. Atul Gupta and others), under Sections 498A,
323, 504, 506, 511, 342, 354, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-III, Varanasi.

sentences.text: 3. Facts of the case are that the opposite party no.2 has lodged an FIR against the applicant and others on 21.12.2018 with the allegations of cruelty and demand of dowry.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: After investigation charge sheet was filed and the Court has taken cognizance vide order dated 02.01.2020.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: He has nothing to do with the present incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: The applicant has been implicated in the present case only to put undue pressure on the husband of opposite party no.2.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

Further,
submission is that no offence against the applicant is disclosed and the court below has utterly failed to consider that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: He also pointed out certain documents in support of his contention.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the application and contended that specific allegation has been made against the applicant in the FIR.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: He further submits that from the perusal of FIR prima facie case is made out against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Court below has rightly taken cognizance against the applicant and no interference is required by this Court in the impugned order as well as the on going proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: All the submissions made at the bar relates to the disputed question of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: At this stage only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
7. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 has laid down the guidelines under which circumstances the Court should, in its inherent power,
entertain an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The guidelines are as follows:-
"(i) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
(ii) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: (iii) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: (iv) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: (v) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49722364/
2 (vi) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: (vii) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fides and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
8. Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs.
State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918, R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192, and lastly, Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs.
Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.) 283 has held that only those cases in which no prima facie case is made out can be considered in an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
9.

sentences.text: The instant application does not fall under the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgements mentioned above, and followed in a number of matters.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: Moreover, the facts as alleged cannot be said that, prima facie, no offence is made out against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2024.json

10. Hence, the instant application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot be entertained and is,
accordingly, dismissed.

2. The instant bail cancellation application has been filed seeking cancellation of the bail granting
order of opposite party no.2 dated 27.08.2024 passed by Additional District and Sessions
Judge/Special Judge (Pocso Act), Bijnor in Case Crime No.186 of 2024, under Sections 363,

sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is the informant of the case and he has filed the instant bail cancellation application on the ground that court concerned wrongly granted bail to opposite party no.2.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: He further submits that from the school record of the victim i.e. daughter of the applicant, it is apparent that she was minor aged about fourteen years and however she in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 did not make any allegation of rape against the opposite party no.2 but from Annexure No.5 of the affidavit, it reflects that opposite party no.2 and victim both have performed marriage and therefore, it reflects that the victim gave her both the statements under pressure and court concerned did not consider this fact.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
5. He further submits that from Annexure No.8 of the affidavit, it reflects that the marriage of the applicant and his wife i.e. parents of the victim was solemnized in the year 2007, therefore, victim cannot be about 21 years old as mentioned by C.M.O. concerned in his report and it reflects that opposite party no.2 anyhow manipulated the C.M.O. concerned and obtained fake age certificate of the victim with regard to her radiological age.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: He further submits that therefore, considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case discussed above bail granted to the opposite party no.2 by the court concerned should be cancelled.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
7. Learned A.G.A. however submits that from the school record, it reflects that victim was minor hardly aged about fourteen years but could not dispute the fact that victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 did not state anything against the opposite party no.2.
8.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
9. From the record, it reflects that as per the school record of the victim, she was around fourteen years of age at the time of alleged incident of rape and as per the report of C.M.O. concerned her radiological age was 21 years but from the record, it also reflects that victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 did not state anything against the opposite party no.2 and after considering this fact court concerned granted bail to opposite party no.2.
10.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, victimin her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 did not state anything against the opposite party no.2 rather she made allegation against applicant i.e. informant of the case (i.e. her father).
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 11. Further, law is settled that it is easy to reject a bail application but it is very difficult to cancel a bail already granted and for cancellation of bail, very cogent and overwhelming reasons are necessary, which in my considered view is missing in the present matter..
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view, the instant bail cancellation application is devoid of merit and is accordingly dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Manoj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024.json
